desc: Read the input values $H, W, X, P, Q$ and the grid $S$. Initialize Takahashi's current strength to $S_{P,Q}$ and mark his starting position as visited/occupied.
Use a min-priority queue to store the strengths of all currently adjacent slimes (initially the 4 neighbors of $(P,Q)$).

Implement a loop that checks the priority queue: if the smallest element in the queue is strictly less than $\text{current\_strength} / X$, pop it, add its value to $\text{current\_strength}$, and add its new neighbors (that haven't been visited yet) to the priority queue.

If the smallest element in the queue is not valid (i.e., $\ge \text{current\_strength} / X$), break the loop as no further moves are possible (since the queue is sorted, larger elements won't be valid either).
Write the complete Python code, ensuring 1-based to 0-based conversion, efficient priority queue usage (`heapq`), and correct neighbor tracking to avoid duplicates and out-of-bounds errors.
